title: Microsoft 365 Copilot connectors: guided OAuth sign-in for connector admins
summary: Pass with documentation gaps: the admin paths and licensing statements are supported. The general pop-up description is not fully documented, and conflicting Microsoft guidance on changing access permissions and federated write actions should be acknowledged.

claims.claim: The guided OAuth experience authorises a connector by consenting in a pop-up flow.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot connectors OAuth pop-up. Opened Gong, GitHub Cloud Knowledge and monday.com deployment pages and release-note excerpts. monday.com documents a pop-up install window; the other pages do not establish pop-up consent as the general mechanism.
claims.fix: Replace the first sentence with: 'Microsoft 365 Copilot connector setup now offers a guided OAuth sign-in, so an admin signs in and grants the connector access to its source system.' The Gong, GitHub and monday.com deployment pages document sign-in and granting access, but not a universal pop-up consent mechanism.

claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft 365 Agents Settings User access tenant agents plugins connectors Microsoft Graph API PowerShell; User access copilot API settings tenant. Read agent-settings and Package Management API overview; package operations do not set tenant-wide User access.

claims.claim: All users is the default option for User access.
claims.quote: **All users** - This option is the default. It means that all users in the organization can access agents and plugins, subject to the existing app policies and user assignments.

claims.claim: User access offers a No users option.
claims.quote: **No users** - This option means that no users in the organization can access agents and plugins.

claims.claim: User access offers a Specific users or groups option.
claims.quote: **Specific users or groups** - This option lets you select specific users or groups in your organization to have access to agents and plugins.

claims.claim: User access governs agents and plugins including connectors, and connector staging cannot widen its user population.
claims.quote: **Agents** > **Settings** > **User access** also applies to connectors. It sets the maximum population of users who can use any connector, regardless of a connector's own staged rollout.

claims.claim: Federated connectors capable of writing to source systems are distinct from the synced connector OAuth authentication change.

The cited federated overview supports write actions, but https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/copilot/connectors/overview#types-of-copilot-connectors still describes federated connectors as read-only alongside an October 2026 write-actions announcement.
